CURRENT (rev 3). GREG, 2026-11-16 about 17:44Z, relayed by Engram::Asistant (mailbox 43498a6e #1396, message 258191f9), verbatim: „Nie. To niech to wejdzie. Clippy poprawione w następnej rundzie. Clippy nie powinno blokowac check-inu. Bledy clippy poprawione w następnej rundzie.” Asistant's scope: this applies to the current dd205 and to both projects. Clippy findings do NOT block a check-in or landing. They are recorded openly, given an owner, and fixed in the next round. They are not a new barrier before work. Existing checks of actual behavior (builds, tests) continue unchanged, and the decision is not extended to other kinds of errors. Kimi agrees a simple rule text with the authors and confirms the rollout, without asking Greg again.
EARLIER (rev 1-2, 17:42Z, #1392/#1394): „Korwa, kiedy wchodzi clippy? Po testach!!! + kimi” led to a practice of running Clippy once on the right platform before the first long run. That practice remains a way to SEE Clippy findings early, but a Clippy failure no longer stops a test run, review or landing.
Practice now: when a run's strict Clippy step reports findings, the run continues to the build and tests (a test build without -D warnings). The findings are filed as an owned next-round fix, and the landing goes ahead when every other required check passes. The rule text and launcher change are owned through Kimi with the authors. As a loosening of a landing condition it lands under the authority-text procedure, with this verbatim word as Greg's widening word.
